title: MDN Web Docs
description: Clear, dependable documentation for HTML, CSS, JavaScript, and the open web platform.
note: Start here when you need an accurate explanation of a browser feature, syntax, or compatibility concern.

title: web.dev
description: Practical guidance for building fast, accessible, and resilient experiences on the web.
note: Especially useful for performance, Core Web Vitals, accessibility, and modern browser capabilities.

title: Can I Use
description: Browser support tables for current and emerging web platform features.
note: Check a feature here before relying on it in production, especially when older browsers matter.

title: GitHub Skills
description: Short, hands-on courses that teach GitHub workflows inside real repositories.
note: A practical choice for learning pull requests, merge conflicts, releases, and automation by doing.

title: The A11Y Project
description: A community-driven collection of accessible web design and development practices.
note: Use the checklists to catch common accessibility mistakes before a site reaches users.

title: Typescale
description: A focused calculator for creating harmonious and responsive typographic scales.
note: Useful during early visual design when headings and body sizes need a consistent relationship.

title: Coolors
description: A quick palette generator with contrast tools and flexible color exploration.
note: Generate options quickly, then validate contrast and adapt the palette to the project’s context.

title: Excalidraw
description: A collaborative sketching canvas for diagrams, flows, wireframes, and quick visual thinking.
note: Its intentionally informal style is ideal for early ideas that should invite discussion, not feel final.

title: roadmap.sh
description: Community-created learning paths for development roles, tools, and technical subjects.
note: Use a roadmap to see the territory, then build projects rather than treating every node as mandatory.

title: The Modern JavaScript Tutorial
description: A structured guide that moves from JavaScript fundamentals to advanced browser concepts.
note: The chapters work well as both a learning sequence and a reference when a concept needs refreshing.

title: regex101
description: An interactive regular-expression editor with explanations, highlighting, and test cases.
note: Choose the correct regex flavor, add representative test strings, and inspect the explanation panel.

title: Bundlephobia
description: A package-size explorer that shows the download cost of npm dependencies.
note: Check dependencies before installation and compare alternatives when page weight is important.

title: Contrast Grid
description: A matrix for testing multiple foreground and background color combinations at once.
note: Paste a working palette to identify accessible pairings without checking each combination manually.

title: Fontsource
description: Open-source font packages designed for self-hosting through common web workflows.
note: Self-hosting can improve privacy and reliability while giving precise control over loaded weights.

title: Carbon
description: A polished code-image generator for presentations, articles, and social sharing.
note: Use it for short, readable excerpts—not as a replacement for accessible code blocks in documentation.

title: diagrams.net
description: A capable diagram editor for architecture, processes, networks, and structured visual models.
note: Best when exact connectors and conventional diagram shapes matter more than a sketch-like feel.

title: Pomofocus
description: A simple browser-based focus timer built around configurable work and break intervals.
note: Keep the session goal small and explicit; the timer is most useful when the next task is already clear.

title: freeCodeCamp
description: A broad collection of free, project-based lessons in web development and programming.
note: Follow a focused certification path and reinforce each section with a small project of your own.
